candidates.sourceLocator: Verstraete and Cirac (2004), arXiv:cond-mat/0407066, abstract: PEPS naturally extend matrix-product constructions to two or more dimensions
candidates.evidenceNote: Projected entangled-pair states extend the matrix-product-state tensor construction to two and higher spatial dimensions within the family of tensor-network ansatzes. This is not a claim of efficient exact representability for every many-body wavefunction.
limitations: Family-level relation, not a theorem that all 2D states are efficiently representable
An ansatz is not a universal exact solver

candidates.sourceLocator: Gottesman, Stabilizer Codes and Quantum Error Correction (1997), thesis abstract on group-theoretic stabilizer code subclass
candidates.evidenceNote: Gottesman's stabilizer formalism gives a group-theoretic description of an important subclass of quantum error-correcting codes. The edge formalizes that subclass, not every possible quantum error-correction scheme.
limitations: Stabilizer codes are a subclass of QEC
The edge does not imply that all QEC has a stabilizer representation

candidates.sourceLocator: He et al., arXiv:1203.2410, abstract: rotating-wave approximation and counter-rotating corrections; cross-check Guo (2009), Phys. Rev. A 80, 033828 abstract
candidates.evidenceNote: The Jaynes–Cummings Hamiltonian is a rotating-wave approximation to the quantum Rabi interaction under appropriate coupling and detuning assumptions. This navigational 'reformulates' edge is not an exact equivalence; omitted counter-rotating terms matter in other regimes.
limitations: Approximation depends on coupling and detuning
No assertion of exact Rabi-JC equivalence or validity at arbitrary ultrastrong coupling
